title: FTMM General Assembly 2025: a year of rebuilding and of a stronger FTMM–ATTP partnership
body_html:
The Table Tennis Federation of the Republic of Moldova closed 2025 with an ordinary General Assembly held on 16 November, at which the year’s results were presented and important decisions were adopted for the stability and modernisation of the federation’s governance. With an unprecedented, historic quorum, the members present approved every resolution on the agenda and endorsed the internal reform process that began in mid-year.

The centrepiece of the meeting was the Annual Activity Report, which confirmed that 2025 was a year of institutional rebuilding: renewed dialogue with national and international authorities, a record number of Board meetings, the restoration of internal legality and a visible rise in sporting performance. The headline result — the national team reaching the last 16 of the European Championships in Zadar and, with it, qualifying for the 2026 World Championships in London — confirms the steady technical progress of Moldovan table tennis.

Significant emphasis was placed on strengthening cooperation between FTMM, ATTP and TOP CUP Academy. Assembly members highlighted the substantial impact of the Super Cup ATTP, Setka Cup and Super League tournaments on growing the player base, the pace of competition and international visibility. 2026 will be the first year in which the Federation benefits from an unprecedented volume of competition, generated largely by its partners and funded from their own resources — proof of ATTP’s maturity and its capacity to support the real development of the sport.

For the ATTP community, this General Assembly confirms that the road to modernising table tennis runs through cooperation, professionalism and mutual trust. The stronger FTMM–ATTP relationship is becoming an essential pillar of sporting and institutional development, and 2026 is shaping up as the year in which the benefits of this collaboration will be more visible than ever.
